name: SWE-Gym
description: The first environment for training software engineering agents, containing 2,438 real-world Python task instances, each comprising a codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language. It also includes SWE-Gym Lite with 230 easier tasks and SWE-Gym Raw with 64,689 Python GitHub issues without executable environments.
creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
citeAs: Pan, J., Wang, X., Neubig, G., Jaitly, N., Ji, H., Suhr, A., & Zhang, Y. (2025). Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym.
rai:dataCollection: SWE-Gym comprises 2,438 real-world software engineering tasks sourced from pull requests in 11 popular Python repositories, constructed in close alignment with SWE-Bench. The authors first used SEART GitHub search to filter repositories created before July 1, 2022 with more than 500 stars, at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests, and 100 contributors, resulting in 358 repositories. They then used SWE-Bench's instance extraction script to convert repositories into task instances corresponding to GitHub issues, including the issue description, repository snapshot, and unit tests, yielding 64,689 instances in SWE-Gym Raw. They semi-manually created executable environments for 11 repositories, manually configured dependencies for each task instance using configuration files, CI scripts, or documentation from the repository snapshot at issue creation time, and validated instances using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script. After filtering failed instances, they obtained 2,438 unit-test-validated instances. A subset of 230 tasks was further selected as SWE-Gym Lite following the SWE-Bench Lite filtering pipeline.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Software Collection, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consist of real-world GitHub issues, repository snapshots, pull requests, codebases, unit tests, and repository metadata from Python repositories on GitHub. SWE-Gym Raw contains 64,689 Python GitHub issue instances spanning 358 repositories without executable environments.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Repositories were selected from those created before July 1, 2022.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors associated instances with version numbers, generalized SWE-Bench's versioning script to support versioning via script execution, and semi-automatically collected versions for each instance based on repository information such as pyproject.toml and git tags. They filtered out failed instances after validation and created a Lite subset by excluding tasks requiring edits to more than one file, poorly described problem statements, excessively complex ground-truth diffs, and tests focused on error message validation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Repositories were filtered using SEART GitHub search criteria. SWE-Bench's instance extraction script was used to create task instances from repositories. Executable environments were then set up by manually configuring dependencies using requirements files, CI scripts, or repository documentation. SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script was used to ensure the gold patch passed more unit tests than the original code. Failed instances were filtered out. For SWE-Gym Lite, the authors followed the SWE-Bench Lite filtering pipeline to exclude multi-file edits, poorly described problems, overly complex diffs, and error-message-focused tests.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual work was used to configure executable environments and verify instances. The authors manually configured dependencies for each task instance using relevant configuration files, CI scripts, or documentation from the repository snapshot at the time of issue creation. They then used SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script to verify that the human-submitted gold patch passed more unit tests than the original code. The paper states that annotations were done by a subset of the authors.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The validation process ensured that the gold patch passed more unit tests than the original code. After validation, failed instances were filtered out, resulting in 2,438 unit-test-validated instances.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: SWE-Bench's instance extraction script; SWE-Bench's versioning script; SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that they publicly release SWE-Gym, models, agent trajectories, and pre-built Docker images for each instance for full reproducibility. No updating timeframe or deprecation policy is specified.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer productivity and accessibility across industries, support critical open-source infrastructure, and make software development more accessible. It also notes potential impacts on software engineering jobs and the need for careful consideration around code ownership, licensing, and attribution. The authors warn that similar techniques could potentially be misused to automate the creation of malicious code and encourage future work on responsible deployment, including security, safety, and economic impacts.
rai:dataBiases: The paper discusses several biases. Ignoring executable environments could introduce distribution bias, diminishing SWE-Gym's utility, so the authors manually configured dependencies to avoid this. The repository distribution exhibits a long-tail pattern, with pandas comprising nearly one-third of the total tasks and bokeh about one percent. In self-improvement experiments, repeated sampling introduces a bias toward easier tasks because task success probability follows a long-tail distribution; training on all successful trajectories is therefore suboptimal. For verifier training, the authors also address easy-data bias by capping the number of successful trajectories per instance.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that SWE-Gym is limited by environment diversity, including the number of repositories, types of tasks, and programming languages. SWE-Gym contains tasks from only 11 Python repositories, while SWE-Gym Raw lacks executable environments. The authors note that tasks in SWE-Gym may be harder than those in SWE-Bench and that current self-improvement results are modest. They also note that current SWE settings focus solely on task completion and neglect human-in-the-loop collaboration.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a training environment for software engineering agents and verifier/reward models. It is used for training language-model-based SWE agents, training verifiers from agent trajectories, inference-time scaling by reranking sampled trajectories, self-improvement experiments, rapid prototyping with SWE-Gym Lite, and future research in SWE agent development and automatic dataset synthesis.
